text:
Eli: Heads-up — small customer reported weird streaming behavior in our sample app: UI shows partial completion then reconnect and shows duplicate final tokens.
Priya: Do we have their repro steps? mobile or desktop?
Maya (mobile-qa): Mobile webview on iOS, intermittent network. Steps: open demo, send 2 long prompt messages back-to-back, then toggle airplane mode for ~1s. Happens ~80% on 14.4 webview.
Sam: Sounds like SSE resume + queued fragments getting replayed? Could be resume token ordering vs chunk sequence.
Eli: I tried repro locally with toggling network in chrome and saw similar: event stream resumed but fragments from before the disconnect arrived out-of-order and final "[DONE]" duplicated.
Priya: Which SDK path? browser fetch-stream or EventSource? sample app uses a fetch + ReadableStream wrapper.
Eli: fetch streaming. We buffer bytes, split by "\n\n" boundaries and parse lines. If a reconnect happens we append new data to buffer.
Sam: That parse approach will merge fragments across reconnects unless we reset state correctly. Are we preserving a resume_id and last_seq?
Maya (mobile-qa): The sample app doesn't include seq numbers in the demo. Customer stream payloads do include "seq" in metadata but our front-end isn't surfacing or validating it.
Priya: Two issues: (1) browser SDK parity — Node SDK had a resume/seq reconstructor for streams but the browser wrapper is naive; (2) mobile webview sometimes fires multiple onopen/onmessage events during flaky handoffs.
Sam: Quick fix: detect reconnect and if server-sent resume token exists, drop any partial fragment and request server to resend from last confirmed seq. Also de-duplicate on seq before rendering.
Eli: Could we add a defensive parser that tolerates duplicate final tokens and ignores repeated completions for same seq? That would be low-risk UX fix.
Priya: Agree. Longer term: expose seq/resume tokens in sample app, and add a small test harness that simulates network toggles (toggle fetch abort + reconnect).
Maya (mobile-qa): I can produce a script using chrome remote debugging to simulate the exact iOS webview behavior and upload a video.
devex-bot: FYI — created issue RED-1182 with stack/steps and attached Maya's repro notes.
Sam: For the browser SDK change, propose: on reconnect, reset byte buffer, rely on server resume token to replay missing messages; enforce idempotency based on (connection_id, seq). Also add a small opt-in 'strictOrdering' flag for apps that want to fail fast on any reordering.
Eli: Implementation note — server already emits "resume_id" and "seq" in comment-prefixed SSE lines: `: resume_id=abc123 seq=42`. We should parse that in browser stream parser.
Priya: We need tests: unit test for split-chunk boundary, integration test that injects duplicate final token and ensures UI shows single completion. Add flaky network scenario to e2e.
Maya (mobile-qa): QA will validate on iOS 13-16 and Android webview. I'll include telemetry showing connection lifecycle events + seq seen.
Sam: I'll open a PR with the defensive de-dupe + seq parse. Will add feature flag and an opt-out for legacy apps.
Eli: Thanks — small doc note for sample app README explaining why seq matters and how to enable strictOrdering please.
Priya: Also add a troubleshooting snippet for customers: how to check server-side resume tokens and validate client-side seq handling.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary of browser-runtime parser v0.21 to staging at 23:00 UTC.
Eli: Perfect — once canary is up we'll run Maya's repro and confirm. If it still happens, attach logs (console + parsed seq) and we can iterate. :thumbsup:
